name: Prize crossword No 24,201
preamble: Method: Solve the clues and fit the solutions in the diagram wherever they will go.

clue.text: Matter for assembly: James (unmarried) observed quietly "wolf's about"

indicators.note: the wolf's word stands about, that is around, the observing and the quiet letters

blocks.note: J is the standard abbreviation for James
unmarried means single, one, and one is the Roman numeral I
to wolf food is to gobble it greedily
observed means saw
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a bachelor called James whispered a warning that a wolf was lurking nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis makes unmarried look like a remark about James, but it is a separate piece. The answer also names the puzzle itself, whose entries are fitted in wherever they will go.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of puzzle is a heap of interlocking cut pieces that have to be put together, so it is literally material waiting to be assembled.

clue.text: Go to synagogue, half magic area that's raised a point

definitions.note: loosely: to judaise is to adopt Jewish practice

indicators.note: half tells you to keep only one of the two equal parts of the magic word

blocks.note: juju is West African magic; only its first half is kept
a dais is a raised platform area in a hall
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: An instruction to attend a synagogue, followed by some muddled stage directions about magic and a raised stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Juju, West African magic, halves neatly into JU and JU.
explanation.definitionFit: To judaise is to conform to Jewish customs and rites, and worshipping at a synagogue is the chief outward sign of doing so.

clue.text: Good German general left off top of tympanum in drain

definitions.note: a grommet is a drain, a small tube through the eardrum

indicators.note: left off says the letter standing for left is dropped from the general's name
top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
Rommel, the Second World War German field marshal, without his L
the opening letter of tympanum

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding picture of something done to the eardrum, with a German general wandering in.
explanation.walkthrough: The tympanum is the eardrum, which is exactly where a grommet goes, so the surface is closer to the answer than it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a tiny tube surgeons fit through the eardrum so fluid from the middle ear can escape, which makes it a drain.

clue.text: I'll be sworn if I 'ad a five foot bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters before it are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, dropped aitch and all
taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five
ft is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A Cockney swears blind that a five-foot bust would be in his possession, if he only had one.
explanation.walkthrough: I'll be sworn sounds like an oath, but the answer is speaking: a document that gets sworn.
explanation.definitionFit: An affidavit is a written statement confirmed by oath before a legal official, so it is a document waiting to be sworn.

clue.text: Pibroch starts with move into wind causing explosion

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of the bagpipe word

blocks.note: pibroch is Highland bagpipe music; its first letter
to luff is to steer a sailing boat closer into the wind

explanation.surface: A piper strikes up and turns into the gale, and the result is a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluff is a Scots word, which suits the bagpipe surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a pluff is a sudden puff or small burst, as of gunpowder going off, hence an explosion.

clue.text: Enthusiastic with German air, talks back vulgarly

indicators.note: back says everything so far is read from right to left

blocks.note: Luft is the German word for air
sez is the slangy spelling of says, which the vulgarly beside it asks for
no letters of its own: it tells you to choose the vulgar spelling of the word for talks

explanation.surface: Someone keen, full of German atmosphere, who answers back rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: Vulgarly tells you to use the slangy spelling sez rather than says.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is keen relish or gusto, so a zestful person approaches things with eager energy, the same as being enthusiastic.

clue.text: Revolt in the course of lengthy Scots eulogising

indicators.note: in the course of puts the revolt inside the Scots word

blocks.note: lang is Scots for long
UDI, a unilateral declaration of independence, is a revolt against the ruling power

explanation.surface: A Scottish uprising during a long-winded speech of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: UDI is best known from Rhodesia's 1965 break with Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauding and eulogising are synonyms: both mean praising someone highly, often in a formal speech.

clue.text: And so wicked queen's books get eaten by fish

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted, so the royal word and the books are rearranged
being eaten puts the jumbled letters inside the fish

blocks.note: a spelling of coley, the coalfish
taken as written
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale ending in which the wicked queen's library is devoured by fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish is given as COLY, a variant of coley.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequently is a connecting adverb meaning as a result, which is what the phrase and so introduces.

clue.text: Love would shortly ebb - the cub gives way to him

definitions.text: the cub gives way to him

indicators.note: an ebb is the tide running the other way, so the word for its opposite is read backwards

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
'ld is an old contracted form of would, as in I'ld
ebb is the reverse of the incoming tide

explanation.surface: A sentimental line about fading love, then a young animal stepping aside for its elder.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Jungle Book the old wolf Akela leads the pack, and Cub Scouts call their leader Akela; a cub defers to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's pack leader is the grizzled senior animal whom the young cubs obey, and Cub Scout packs borrowed his name for their adult leader.

clue.text: Food after sunset failing to bond?

indicators.note: set can mean arranged, so the three letters before it are put into a new order
food after the other piece means the food word is placed second, though the clue mentions it first

blocks.note: read as two words, sun and set; sun is the letters to be used and set is the instruction to rearrange them
tuck is British schoolboy slang for food, especially sweets and snacks

explanation.surface: Someone eating after sunset, perhaps breaking a fast, as glue fails to hold.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunset reads as one word, but it splits into the word sun and an instruction to set its letters anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes unstuck has lost its adhesion, so it has failed to stay bonded; the phrase also means plans going wrong.

clue.text: Instruction at junction: kerb this side needs repair

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so the letters must be rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A road sign at a crossroads warning that the kerb on this side is damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Junction looks like a road junction to match kerb, but it is a joining of two people in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: At the end of a wedding the officiant tells the groom he may now do this, an instruction given at the joining of a couple.

clue.text: Went to heaven drinking m-m-milk?

definitions.note: describes milk rather than naming it, as the question mark signals

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so the stammered letters go into the heavenward word

blocks.note: skied (or skyed) means hit high into the sky, as with a cricket ball
the stammered letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A stuttering soul ascends to heaven while drinking milk.
explanation.walkthrough: Went to heaven suggests dying, but it means sent skywards, as a batsman skies a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimmed is the kind of milk with the cream taken off the top, so it is a type of milk, defined by example.

clue.text: Period whose forte provided links

blocks.note: f is the musical abbreviation for forte, loud
provided can mean on condition that, if
ties are things that link or bind

explanation.surface: A historical era whose particular strength lay in making connections.
explanation.walkthrough: Forte looks like strength, but here it is the musical loud mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifties is a decade, such as the 1950s, which is a span of time and so a period.

clue.text: Search for unique status

indicators.note: the answer is found standing for, in place of, part of the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a special position in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A quest is a long search for something valued, as in the knights' pursuit of the Grail.

clue.text: Flare like a feather

blocks.note: first meaning: a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor Edward Very
second meaning: weighing almost nothing

explanation.walkthrough: The capital V of the signal flare is hidden by the phrase being split differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is a pistol-fired signal flare, and a feather weighs next to nothing, so the phrase fits both.

clue.text: First things to grasp: little beasts accept money

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the coin goes inside the small animals

blocks.note: runts are the smallest animals of a litter
a dime is a ten-cent US coin

explanation.surface: Basic advice: first, get hold of the small creatures, and let them take the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudiments are the basic principles of a subject, the elementary things a learner must understand before anything else.

clue.text: With wild ibex the identification should be displayed

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so these letters run loose and regroup

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
ID is the usual short form of identification

explanation.surface: A zoo notice: a wild mountain goat must have its identification label on view.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhibited and displayed both mean put on show for others to see, as in a gallery or museum.

clue.text: House share with philosopher?

definitions.note: Hamlet links him with philosophy, as the question mark hints

blocks.note: ho is the abbreviation for house
a ratio is a proportional share

explanation.surface: An invitation to share a house with a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet tells his friend there are more things in heaven and earth than are dreamt of in your philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's scholarly friend from Wittenberg is the one addressed about his philosophy, so the setter playfully calls him a philosopher.

clue.text: Reserve gets goal with supporter on shelf

blocks.note: to book is to reserve
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A football picture: the substitute scores, with a fan sitting on the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: Reserve, goal and supporter all point to football, but none of them is about the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookend is a heavy prop placed at the end of a row of volumes on a shelf to hold them upright.

clue.text: End without side in the South

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the end word goes round the team

blocks.note: to die is to come to an end
a side is a team of eleven, as in cricket or football, written XI

explanation.surface: A gloomy note about the end of a team in the South.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like it means lacking, but it is the old word for outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixie is a nickname for the southern states of the US, familiar from the song Dixie.

clue.text: Conservative enters needing only half animals

indicators.note: enters puts the political letter inside the golfing term

blocks.note: in golf, a player is dormie when as many holes up as remain, so needs only a half to win
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Conservative entering a contest needing only half the votes.
explanation.walkthrough: A half in golf is a tied hole, which is all a dormie player needs from each of the remaining ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small nocturnal rodents famous for hibernating, so they are a kind of animal; the definition is the broad class.

clue.text: The yellow flower of Troy - unknown one?

definitions.text: The yellow flower of Troy - unknown one?

blocks.note: surface reading: a golden bloom growing at ancient Troy
setter's reading: a flower is something that flows, a river whose Greek name means yellow; in Homer it is the name the gods use, while men call the river Scamander, so mortals do not know it

explanation.walkthrough: Flower here means something that flows: a river. Homer says the gods call it by this name while men call it Scamander.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan river's divine name comes from the Greek for yellow, and it was a name hidden from mortals, hence unknown.

clue.text: Ice cream is wrong on its opening

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
taken as written
first letter of its

explanation.surface: A complaint that the ice cream has been wrongly served at its launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortoni is an Italian-style frozen dessert of cream, almonds and macaroons, a type of ice cream.

clue.text: The child is a girl

blocks.note: taken as written
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A simple announcement at a birth: the baby is a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a complete sentence, but its second half splits into a word and a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is the formal legal word for offspring, so a child is one's issue.

clue.text: Silas covers one with salt

indicators.note: covering something means going round it, so the novel's hero goes round the number

blocks.note: Silas Marner is the weaver in George Eliot's novel of that name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cook named Silas sprinkles salt over a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt looks like seasoning, but an old salt is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned seaman, and a mariner is likewise a sailor, so the two are slang and formal names for one job.

clue.text: Talks too much Scots - try eats for a change

indicators.note: making a change means the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chatty Scot urged to try eating, perhaps to keep their mouth busy.
explanation.definitionFit: To yatter is Scots for to chatter idly and at length, so a person who does this is talking far too much.

clue.text: Made beastly remark audible in Grenada

indicators.note: audible means we go by how the island's name is pronounced, and only part of it, not how it is written

blocks.note: the island is said gre-NAY-da, and its middle syllables carry the sound

explanation.surface: Someone said something rude and it was overheard on the Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The island Grenada, unlike the Spanish city, is pronounced with a long A, which is what makes the hidden sound work.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse neighs, so making the noise of a beast is exactly what neighing is; beastly plays on its rude sense.

clue.text: Quality of Mendelssohn's "Songs of Silence"

blocks.note: surface reading: praise for the excellence of a set of quiet pieces by the composer
setter's reading: Mendelssohn's piano pieces are called Songs without Words, and the quality they share is having no lyrics

explanation.walkthrough: Quality reads as excellence, but it means a characteristic. Mendelssohn's famous piano pieces are titled Songs without Words.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces titled as songs that have no lyrics share the characteristic of lacking any text, the abstract noun for having no speech.
